# Photutils Astronomical Photometry

Curated by Skill Harbor — a working guide to Photutils, the modern Astropy-coordinated package for extracting quantitative data from astronomical images: estimating and subtracting complex 2D sky backgrounds, detecting stars and galaxies (DAOStarFinder, IRAFStarFinder, segmentation), measuring brightness with circular/elliptical/rectangular apertures, fitting PSF models in crowded fields, computing precise centroids, and running isophotal analysis on galaxy shapes — with the core principles that make photometry trustworthy (background first, aperture vs. PSF trade-offs, units-aware WCS apertures). Discovered via skills.sh, listed here with credit to its creator by @tondevrel. Honest caveats: requires Python with photutils installed; assumes you have astronomical images to analyze (it replaces legacy tools like SExtractor/DAOPHOT, not your telescope); 46 installs on the catalog, but popularity is not a review. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Not verified.
